```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# HTML figures are drawn as PNG and kept as WebP: lossless, or lossy at quality 90 when that is less than half the
# size. The PDF figures stay vector graphics. Any failure of magick (not installed, no WebP, or a broken
# installation whose system libraries are missing) keeps the PNG
webp <- function(path) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output() || !grepl(pattern = "[.]png$", x = path)) return(path)
  tryCatch(
      {
        if (!requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE) || !isTRUE(magick::magick_config()$webp)) return(path)
        img <- magick::image_read(path)
        out <- sub(pattern = "[.]png$", replacement = ".webp", x = path)
        tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".webp")
        magick::image_write(
            image   = img
          , path    = out
          , format  = "webp"
          , quality = 100
          , defines = c(`webp:lossless` = "true")
          )
        magick::image_write(image = img, path = tmp, format = "webp", quality = 90)
        if (file.size(tmp) < file.size(out) / 2) file.copy(from = tmp, to = out, overwrite = TRUE)
        unlink(c(path, tmp))
        out
      }
    , error = function(e) path
    )
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = FALSE, comment = "", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2,
                      dev = if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "cairo_pdf" else "ragg_png", dpi = 96,
                      fig.process = webp)
if (requireNamespace("VetResearchLMM", quietly = TRUE)) library(VetResearchLMM) else
  pkgload::load_all(export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
```


# Abstract

Every example of Chapters 1 and 2 of Duchateau, Janssen and Rowlands (1998), with the SAS program of Appendix B,
the same analysis with **VetResearchLMM**, and the numbers printed in the book next to the computed ones. All of them
agree (the variance 3.685 of Example 2.4.3.1 is printed truncated; it is 3.6855).

```{r ref}
ref <-
  vlm_reference(
      source   = NULL
    , evaluate = TRUE
    , level    = 1
    )
show_ref <- function(pattern) {
  r <- ref[grepl(pattern = pattern, x = ref$source)]
  knitr::kable(x = r[, c("quantity", "value", "computed", "agrees")], digits = 4,
               col.names = c("Quantity", "Book", "Computed", "Agrees"))
}
```

# Example 1.3.2: expected mean squares

Drugs were given to whole herds and doses to animals (`ex124`). With herd random, drug must be tested against herd
within drug, as the expected mean squares show; when one animal is removed, the two expected mean squares no longer
match (9.7143 against 9.7222) and the F test becomes approximate, one reason to prefer the mixed model.

```{r}
em1 <-
  vlm_ems(
      fixed  = PCVdif ~ drug + drug:herd + dose + dose:drug
    , data   = ex124[-1, ]
    , random = ~ drug:herd
    , type   = 3
    , class  = "herd"
    )
em1
show_ref("Table 1.3.2")
```

# Example 2.2.1.7: one-way analysis of variance

```{r}
f2217 <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = PCVdiff ~ dose
    , data     = ex121
    , random   = NULL
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr")
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
vlm_estimate(
    fit    = f2217
  , L      = list("l vs mh" = list(dose = c(-0.5, 1, -0.5)))
  , random = NULL
  , level  = 0.95
  )
show_ref("2.2.1")
```

# Section 2.3.2: the models of Chapter 1

The randomised blocks of `ex122`, the herds nested in drug of `ex123` and the ELISA data of `ex126`, where animals
and times are random and the mean is the only fixed effect:

```{r}
f126 <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = OD ~ 1
    , data     = ex126
    , random   = ~ anim_id + time
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr")
    , type     = 3
    , class    = "time"
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
f126$covariance
```

# Example 2.4.2.2: ML and REML

```{r}
ml <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "ML"
    , ddfm     = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr")
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
reml <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr")
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
data.frame(
    component = reml$covariance$parameter
  , ML        = ml$covariance$estimate
  , REML      = reml$covariance$estimate
  )
show_ref("Table 2.4.2.1")
```

# Example 2.4.3.1: best linear unbiased prediction

```{r}
fs <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Ww ~ 1
    , data     = ex127
    , random   = ~ sire
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr")
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
vlm_blup(
    fit   = fs
  , level = 0.95
  )
show_ref("2.4.3.1")
```

# Examples 2.5.1.1 to 2.5.4.1: fixed effects, estimates and inference spaces

```{r}
fm <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
fm$fixed
vlm_estimate(
    fit    = fm
  , L      = list(
        "broad"  = list(Intercept = 1, Drug = c(0, 1), dose = c(0.5, 0.5), "Drug:dose" = c(0, 0, 0.5, 0.5))
      , "narrow" = list(Intercept = 1, Drug = c(0, 1), dose = c(0.5, 0.5), "Drug:dose" = c(0, 0, 0.5, 0.5))
      )
  , random = list("narrow" = list(Region = rep(1 / 6, 6), "Region:Drug" = rep(c(0, 1 / 6), 6)))
  , level  = 0.95
  )
show_ref("2\\.5\\.|Table 2\\.5")
```

# Example 2.6.1: general linear hypotheses

```{r}
vlm_contrast(
    fit = fm
  , L   = list(
        "all" = list(
            list(Drug = c(1, -1), "Drug:dose" = c(0.5, 0.5, -0.5, -0.5))
          , list(dose = c(1, -1), "Drug:dose" = c(0.5, -0.5, 0.5, -0.5))
          , list("Drug:dose" = c(0.5, -0.5, -0.5, 0.5))
          )
      )
  )
show_ref("2.6.1")
```
